title: Maximum-Sum Bounded Subarray Length
statement_html:
Given a sequence of n integers a and an integer k, consider all non-empty contiguous subarrays whose length is at most k.

Find the length of a subarray with the maximum possible sum. If several eligible subarrays have the same maximum sum, print the greatest length among them.

Your algorithm should run in linear time.

Input: the first line has n and k; the second line has a[0..n-1].

Output: one integer: the greatest length among all maximum-sum non-empty subarrays of length at most k.

Example 1:

Input:
7 4
-2 3 1 -5 4 6 -1
Output: 2
Explanation: The maximum sum is 10, from the subarray [4, 6] of length 2.

Example 2:

Input:
5 3
1 0 0 -5 1
Output: 3
Explanation: The maximum sum is 1. Both [1] and [1, 0, 0] have it; the greatest length is 3.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n < 106

  • 1 <= k <= n

  • -1015 <= a[i] <= 1015

  • Sums can exceed 64 bits; the reference C++ solution uses __int128 internally.

Similar to the 3 Sep class problem "Maximum-Sum Subarray with Length Constraints" (at most k case) and LeetCode #53. Maximum Subarray (differs in: length at most k, and the greatest length is reported).
